scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the ticket: models/actions/factory/migrations for the feature, plus the three docs the task explicitly requires (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md). No unrelated refactors or new features; UI/totem work is correctly left out.

issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new behavior, violating the project's mandatory test-first rule and leaving the daily/prefix sequence, map validation, UpdateQueue error path, migration backfill/index replacement and factory day handling entirely unverified.

The value check preg_match('/^[A-Z]$/', $value) accepts a string such as "A\n" because PHP's '$' matches before a trailing newline, so a map value can bypass the 'exactly one uppercase letter' rule and produce a malformed code prefix.

An explicitly supplied issue_date is always overwritten with the date of issued_at (which defaults to now()), so Ticket::factory()->create(['issue_date' => '2026-09-28']) silently becomes today; because the task says issue_date 'defaults to' the issued_at date, an explicit value arguably should be honoured (tests currently must pass issued_at instead).

DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP is declared but never used (defaultPrefixFor hardcodes the letters and can drift from it), and nextCode's int/numeric-string priority resolution is dead code relative to this change because both callers pass an already-resolved prefix letter, adding an unused DB-lookup branch.

The issued_at/issue_date date-resolution logic is duplicated between the factory callback and the Ticket creating hook and is nested four levels deep; a small shared helper would keep the factory focused on code allocation.

The backfill runs one UPDATE per ticket (chunkById plus a per-row update); a single set-based UPDATE ... SET issue_date = DATE(issued_at) would be simpler and faster, with the PHP fallback only needed for unparsable values.

review.summary: The change implements the priority-prefix map, per-prefix daily sequence, issue_date migration, factory alignment, UpdateQueue parameter and docs largely correctly and within scope, with only minor edge-case and dead-code issues. It cannot be approved as is because a domain change of this size ships no tests at all, which the project's test-first convention makes mandatory; add coverage for sequence/restart, malformed codes, map validation, UpdateQueue failures, migration backfill and factory day alignment.
